newsitem.title: USA: IMF-World Bank panel endorses debt relief plan.
newsitem.headline: IMF-World Bank panel endorses debt relief plan.

text.p: The International Monetary Fund-World Bank Development Committee Monday endorsed a plan to help heavily indebted poor countries reduce their debt burdens and recommended that the two lending institutions begin its implementation before the end of this year.
In a communique released following a meeting of the Development Committee, it urged the bank and Fund, working closely with donors and other creditors, "to move swiftly to implement the initiative."
The communique said the committee recognized the initiative "commits the international financial community to take additional action to reduce eligible countries' debt burdens to sustainable levels."
The communique stressed that the initiative should be implemented flexibly, on a case-by-case basis, and with full participation by debtor governments.

The communique also said the Development Committee ministers welcomed "the indication" from the Paris Club that it was ready to go beyond Naples terms to provide debt reduction of up to 80 percent for qualifying countries. The current Naples terms provide 67 percent debt reduction.

Noting that the International Development Association replenishment agreement reflects "significant reduction" in donor contributions from previous levels, the committee asked IDA management and donors "to work together in the next several months to help ensure adequate and secure funding for IDA."
